The meaning of their being given their reward twice is that they will have, for obedience, twice what other women deserve if they perform that same obedience.

In this there is a strong proof that the meaning of ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, double﴾ is that the punishment will be twice, not thrice, because the purpose is to show their nobility and distinction in obedience and disobedience: their good deed counts as two good deeds, and their evil deed as two evil deeds. Had their evil deed been like three evil deeds, it would not fit that their good deed be like two good deeds, for Allah is too just to multiply the punishment for them to a degree exceeding the multiplication of their reward. ﴿And We have prepared for her﴾, in addition to the double reward, ﴿a generous provision﴾.

The exegetes said: the generous provision is the bounty of Paradise; al-Nahhas related this from them.

Then He, glory be to Him, made their excellence over all other women explicit, saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of the women﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: He did not say "like one of the women," because "ahad" is a general negation applying to the masculine and feminine, the singular and plural. It may be said of what is not human, as one says: "There is no one (ahad) in it, neither sheep nor camel."

The meaning: you are not like a single group among the groups of women in virtue and nobility.

Then He restricted this great nobility by a condition, saying: ﴿if you fear Allah﴾. Thus He, glory be to Him, made clear that this excellence for them is only by their steadfast adherence to piety (taqwa), not by mere connection to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Clear piety, sincere faith, and walking in the manner of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his life and after his death have indeed been found in them, all praise be to Allah.

The response to the condition is omitted, being indicated by what precedes it, meaning: if you fear Allah, then you are not like any one of the women.

It has been said that its response is ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾ (fa-la takhdhna), but the first is preferable.

The meaning of ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾ is: do not make your speech soft when addressing people, as the women of ill repute do, for that causes a great corruption, namely ﴿so that one in whose heart is a disease may covet﴾ — that is, immorality, doubt and hypocrisy. The accusative of "yatma'a" is because it is the response to the prohibition. The majority read it thus.

Abu Hatim related that al-A'raj read "fa-yat'ami'" with a fathah on the yaʾ and a kasrah on the mim. Al-Nahhas said: I reckon this is an error. This reading is related from Abu al-Sammal, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Muhaysin, and it is related from them that they read it in the jussive, coordinated with the position of the prohibitive verb.

﴿And speak a known word﴾ — among the people, far from doubt, according to the ways of the Sharia, such that its hearer finds nothing objectionable in it, and the people of wickedness and immorality do not covet them because of it.

﴿And stay in your houses﴾ (wa-qarna fi buyutikunna). The majority read "wa-qirna" with a kasrah on the qaf, from waqara yaqiru waqaran, meaning: to be settled. The imperative of it is "qir" with a kasrah on the qaf, and for women: "qirna", like "idna" and "zinna".

Al-Mubarrad said: it is from al-qarar, not from al-waqar. You say "qarartu bi-l-makan" with a fathah on the ra', and the original is "iqrirna" with a kasrah on the ra'. The first ra' was dropped for lightness, as they said in "zaliltu" → "zalt", and they transferred its vowel to the qaf, and the hamzat al-wasl was dispensed with by moving the qaf.

Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: the first ra' was changed into a yaʾ out of dislike of gemination, as it was changed in qirat and dinar, and the yaʾ took the vowel of the letter from which it was changed. The underlying form is "iqirna," then the vowel of the yaʾ is cast onto the qaf, out of dislike of moving the yaʾ with a kasrah, so the yaʾ falls for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the hamzat al-wasl falls because what follows it is moved, so it becomes "qarna".

Nafi' and ʿAsim read with a fathah on the qaf, and its root is "qarirtu bi-l-makan" when you stayed in it, with a kasrah on the ra', "aqarru" with a fathah on the qaf, like "hamida yahmadu". This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; Abu ʿUbayd related this from al-Kisa'i, and al-Zajjaj and others mentioned it.

Al-Farra' said: it is like when you say "hal hassta sahibaka," meaning: did you perceive him? Abu ʿUbayd said: our teachers among the people of Arabic used to deny the reading with a fathah on the qaf, because "qarirtu bi-l-makan aqarru" is not permitted by many of the people of Arabic.

The sound form is "qarartu aqirru" with a kasrah, and its meaning is the command to them to be dignified and calm in their houses and not to go out. This contradicts what we have mentioned here from him, from al-Kisa'i, and he is one of his most eminent teachers.

Abu Hatim concurred in denying this reading, saying: "qarna" with a fathah on the qaf has no standing in the language of the Arabs.

Al-Nahhas said: Abu Hatim has been contradicted in his claim that it has no standing in the speech of the Arabs; rather there are two usages in it: one related by al-Kisa'i, and the other from ʿAli ibn Sulayman. As for the usage related by al-Kisa'i, it is what we have already mentioned from the narration of Abu ʿUbayd from him. As for the usage related by ʿAli ibn Sulayman, he said: it is from "qarartu bihi ʿaynan, aqarru," and the meaning: "and be comforted with it in your eyes in your houses." Al-Nahhas said: this is a good form.

I say: it is not good, nor is it the meaning of the verse, for what is intended by it is their being commanded to tranquillity and settling in their houses, and this has nothing to do with the coolness of the eye.

Ibn Abi ʿAblah read "wa-qirna" with an alif of wasl and two ra's, the first with a kasrah according to the original.

﴿And do not display yourselves in the manner of the former time of ignorance (tabarruj al-jahiliyyah al-ula)﴾. Tabarruj is that a woman reveals of her adornment and beauties what she is obliged to cover, of that which excites a man's desire. The meaning of tabarruj has already been mentioned in Surah al-Nur.

Al-Mubarrad said: it is taken from breadth; one says: "in his teeth there is a barej," when they are spaced apart. It has been said: tabarruj is swaggering in walking, but this is very weak.

It has been differed over what is meant by "the former time of ignorance": it has been said: the period between Adam and Noah; it has been said: between Noah and Idris; it has been said: between Noah and Abraham; it has been said: between Moses and Jesus; and it has been said: between Jesus and Muhammad.

Al-Mubarrad said: "al-Jahiliyyah al-Ula" is like saying "al-Jahiliyyah al-Jahla' (the utter ignorance)."

He said: The women of the Jahiliyyah used to display what is ugly to display, to the point that a woman would sit with her husband and her paramour, and her paramour would be alone with what is above the waist-wrap upward, while her husband would be alone with what is below it downward; and at times one of them would ask the other for an exchange.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: What appears to me is that He meant the Jahiliyyah that they had reached, from which they were commanded to shift away from their conduct in it, namely what was before the Sharia of the conduct of the disbelievers, because they had no jealousy (ghayrah) among them. The meaning is not that there is another Jahiliyyah; so he said, and it is a good opinion.

It is possible that by the other Jahiliyyah is meant what occurs in Islam of imitating the people of the Jahiliyyah by word or deed. The meaning then is: "And do not display yourselves, O Muslim women, after your Islam, with a display like the display of the Jahiliyyah in which you were, and which was upon those before you." That is: do not produce, by your actions and your words, a Jahiliyyah resembling the Jahiliyyah that was before. ﴿And establish the prayer, give the zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. He singled out the prayer and the zakah because they are the foundation of the bodily and financial acts of obedience.

Then He generalized, commanding them to obey Allah and His Messenger in everything that is Sharia. ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾. That is: Allah has only enjoined upon you what He has enjoined of piety, that you not be soft in speech, that you speak what is customary (ma'ruf), that you remain in your houses, that you not display yourselves, that you establish the prayer and give the zakah, and obey; so that He may remove from you the impurity, O people of the House. By "ar-rijs" (impurity) is meant sin and wrongdoing, which defile honor, arising from abandoning what Allah has commanded and doing what He has forbidden; so everything in which there is no pleasure of Allah falls under that.

The accusative of "Ahl al-Bayt" is in the sense of praise (al-madh), as al-Zajjaj said; and he said: if you wish, it is in apposition (badal). He said: the nominative and genitive are also permissible.

al-Nahhas said: If it is in the genitive, it is in apposition to the kaf and mim (of "ankum" and "yutahhirakum"). al-Mubarrad objected that apposition from the addressed is not permissible; and it is permissible that it be in the accusative by way of address (nida')... ﴿and purify you with a thorough purification﴾. That is: He will purify you from the filths and defilements with complete purification.

In the metaphor of "rijs" for disobedience, and in following it with "purification," there is an eloquent repulsion from it and a severe deterrence for its doer.

The people of knowledge have differed about the People of the House mentioned in the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the People of the House mentioned in the verse are exclusively the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).

They said: By "the house" is meant the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the dwellings of his wives, due to His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses﴾.

Also, the context concerns the wives, from His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives...﴿ up to His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah and the wisdom; indeed Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Mujahid, Qatadah, and it was reported from al-Kalbi, said that the People of the House mentioned in the verse are: 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn exclusively. Among their proofs is that the address in the verse is with what suits the masculine, not the feminine, namely His saying: "'ankum" and "liyutahhirakum." Had it been exclusively for the women, He would have said "'ankunna" and "yutahhirukunna."

The earlier ones answered this: the masculine is by consideration of the word "Ahl" (people), as He, glorified be He, said: (p-1168) ﴿Do you wonder at the command of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the House﴾ [Hud: 73], and as a man says to his companion: "How is your family?" meaning his wife or wives, and he replies: "They are well."

Let us mention here what each group held to: As for the first, they held to the context, for it concerns the wives as we mentioned, and to what Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) exclusively.

'Ikrimah said: Whoever wishes, I will invoke a mubahalah (mutual curse) with him that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated similar from the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Ikrimah similar. Ibn Sa'd narrated from 'Urwah similar.

As for what the others held to: al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, through several routes: "From Umm Salamah who said: In my house it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾, and in the house were Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) covered them with a cloak that was upon him, then said: 'These are my People of the House, so remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated "from Umm Salamah also, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in her house on his bed, upon which was a Khaybari cloak. Fatimah came with a pot in which was khazirah (a dish of meat and grain), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Call your husband and your two sons, al-Hasan and al-Husayn,' and she called them. While they were eating, there was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) took the remnant of his cloak and covered them with it, then he extended his hand out of the cloak and raised it toward the sky, then said: 'O Allah, these are my People of the House and my close ones, so remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification,' saying it three times.

Umm Salamah said: I put my head into the curtain and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and am I with you?' He said: 'You are upon goodness, twice.'" Ahmad also narrated it from her narration, saying: "Narrated 'Abdullah ibn Numayr to us, narrated 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman to us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, narrated to me one who heard Umm Salamah mention that the Prophet (ﷺ)..." and he mentioned it.

In its chain is an unknown narrator, who is the teacher of 'Ata', and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.

al-Tabarani also narrated it from her through two routes with similar wording.

Ibn Kathir in his tafsir mentioned for the hadith of Umm Salamah many routes in the Musnad of Ahmad and others.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib narrated similar from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh again narrated from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, stepson of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: When this verse was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾, and he mentioned something like the hadith of Umm Salamah.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated from 'A'ishah who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) went out one morning wearing a black-haired striped cloak of wool. Al-Hasan and al-Husayn came, and he admitted them with him; then Fatimah came, and he admitted her with him; then 'Ali came, and he admitted him with him; then he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Fatimah, and with him were 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, until he entered. He brought 'Ali and Fatimah near and seated them before him, and seated al-Hasan and al-Husayn each upon one of his thighs. Then he wrapped his garment around them, while I was behind them. Then he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾ and said: 'O Allah, these are my People of the House; O Allah, remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and am I from your family?' He said: 'And you are from my family.'"

Wathilah said: "Indeed, it is more hopeful than what I hope for." It has routes in the Musnad of Ahmad.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi who graded it hasan, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas: "That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pass by the door of Fatimah when he went out to the dawn prayer, saying: 'The prayer, O People of the House, the prayer! ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾'"

Muslim narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I remind you of Allah regarding my People of the House." It was said to Zayd: "And who are his People of the House? Are not his wives from his People of the House?" He said: "His wives are from his People of the House, but his People of the House are those who are forbidden the charity after him: the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of al-'Abbas."

al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed Allah divided creation into two divisions, and placed me in the better of the two divisions. That is His saying: ﴿And the companions of the right hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 7] ﴿And the companions of the left hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 41]; so I am of the companions of the right, and I am the best of the companions of the right. Then He made the two divisions into thirds, and placed me in the best of them as three. That is His saying: ﴿So the companions of the right hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 8] ﴿and the companions of the left hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 9] ﴿and the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 10]; so I am of the foremost, and I am the best of the foremost. Then He made the thirds into tribes, and placed me in the best tribe. That is His saying: ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13]; and I am the most righteous and the most honored of the children of Adam before Allah, and no boast. Then He made the tribes into houses, and placed me in the best house. That is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification﴾. So I and the People of my House are purified from sins.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Hamra' who said: "I stayed in Madinah for seven months during the time of the Messenger of Allah. I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the dawn rose, come to the door of 'Ali and Fatimah and say: 'The prayer, the prayer! ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾'"

In its chain is Abu Dawud al-A'ma, who is a fabricator and a liar (wada' kadhdhab).

There are in this chapter hadiths and reports; and we have mentioned here what is suitable to be relied upon, apart from what is not suitable.

A third group has moderated between the two groups, making this verse inclusive of the wives and of 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. As for the wives, it is because they are the ones intended in the context of these verses, as we previously stated, and because they are the ones dwelling in his houses (ﷺ), descending in his dwellings; and what was previously reported from Ibn 'Abbas and others supports this. As for the inclusion of 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, it is because they are his relatives and his People of the House by lineage. What we have mentioned of the hadiths explicitly stating that they were the cause of revelation supports this. Whoever makes the verse exclusive to one of the two groups has acted upon part of what must be acted upon and neglected what must not be neglected.

This view has been preferred by a group of verifiers, among them al-Qurtubi, Ibn Kathir, and others.

And some scholars said: they are the Banu Hashim. They relied on the hadith of Ibn Abbas mentioned earlier, and on the statement of Zayd ibn Arqam mentioned earlier, where he said: "But his family are those who were deprived of charity after him: the family of Ali, the family of Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of al-Abbas." These scholars held that what is meant by "the house" is the house of lineage.

His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾. That is: remember the favour of Allah when He placed you in houses where the verses of Allah and wisdom are recited. Remember them, reflect upon them, so that you may be admonished by the admonitions of Allah. Or remember them for the people, so that they may take admonition from them and be guided by their guidance. Or remember them by reciting them, so that you may memorise them and not cease to recite them frequently.

Al-Qurtubi said: The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said: "The verses of Allah" are the Qur'an, and "wisdom" is the Sunnah (the prophetic practice and teaching).

Muqatil said: What is meant by "the verses and wisdom" is His command and prohibition in the Qur'an.

It was also said: the Qur'an combines being clear verses, indicating the Oneness of God and the truth of prophethood, and being wisdom, comprising various branches of knowledge and laws.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾. That is: Subtle towards His friends, Acquainted with all His creation and with everything that proceeds from them, whether good or evil, obedience or disobedience. He rewards the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.

Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, through the route of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: "Abu Bakr came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while people were sitting at his door and the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting, but he was not granted permission. Then Umar came and sought permission, but he was not granted permission. Then permission was given to Abu Bakr and Umar, and they entered while the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting with his wives around him, and he was silent. Umar said: 'I will speak to the Prophet (ﷺ), perhaps he will laugh.' Then Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen the daughter of Zayd, the wife of Umar, when she asked me for maintenance a moment ago, and I struck her on the neck.' The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, and said: 'They are around me, asking me for maintenance.' Abu Bakr then got up to Aisha to strike her, and Umar got up to Hafsa, both saying: 'You ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for what he does not have.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them. His wives said: 'By Allah, we will not ask the Messenger of Allah for what he does not have after this gathering.' And Allah revealed the option (of choice). He called Aisha and said: 'I am going to mention to you a matter, and I do not want you to hasten in it until you consult your two parents.' She said: 'What is it?' Then he recited to her ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives...﴾ to the end of the verse. Aisha said: 'Concerning you, should I consult my parents? Rather, I choose Allah and His Messenger, and I ask you not to mention to your wives what I have chosen.' He said: 'Indeed Allah did not send me as one who causes difficulty, but He sent me as a teacher and a bringer of good news. None of them will ask me about what you have chosen except that I will inform her.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "came to her when Allah commanded him to give his wives the choice. She said: He began with me and said: 'I am going to mention to you a matter, and there is no harm for you in not hastening until you consult your two parents.' And he knew that my parents would not have commanded me to separate from him. He said: 'Indeed Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world...﴾' to the end of the verse. I said to him: 'Then in which of these should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode.' And the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) did the same as I did."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever of you is devoutly obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness﴾, that he said: "That is: whoever of you obeys Allah, and whoever of you does deeds for Allah and His Messenger by obeying Him."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him concerning His saying: ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾, that he said: "That is: do not make your speech alluring, and do not be soft in speech."

Ibn al-Mundhir also transmitted from him, concerning the same verse: "It is the softening of speech with men, until the one in whose heart is a disease becomes eager."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "I was informed that it was said to Sawda, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'What is wrong with you that you do not perform Hajj or 'Umrah as your sisters do?' She said: 'I have performed Hajj and 'Umrah, and Allah has commanded me to remain in my house. By Allah, I will not leave my house until I die.' He said: 'By Allah, she did not leave the door of her chamber until she was carried out on her bier.'"

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Sa'd, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Zuhd, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Masruq, who said: "Whenever Aisha recited ﴿And stay in your houses﴾, she would weep until her head-covering was soaked."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman transmitted: "The first jahiliyya (age of ignorance, the pre-Islamic period of unbelief) was between Noah and Idris, and it was a thousand years."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas that Umar ibn al-Khattab asked him: "Tell me about the saying of Allah to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And do not display yourselves as in the first jahiliyya﴾. Was there more than one jahiliyya?" Ibn Abbas said: "I have not heard of a 'first' except that it has a 'last'." Umar said to him: "Bring me from the Book of Allah what confirms that." He said: "Allah says: ﴿And strive in Allah with the striving due to Him; He has chosen you﴾ [al-Hajj 22:78] as the first time." Umar said: "Who commanded us to strive?" He said: "Makhzum and Abd Shams."

Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning the verse, that he said: "There will be another jahiliyya." Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Aisha that she recited this verse and said: "The first jahiliyya was in the time of Abraham." Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The first jahiliyya was between Jesus and Muhammad."

We have already mentioned the reports concerning the occasion of revelation of His saying: ﴿Allah only desires to remove from you the impurity, O people of the house﴾.

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾, that he said: "It is the Qur'an and the Sunnah (the Prophet's practice), by which He bestows favour upon them."

Ibn Sa'd transmitted from Abu Umama, from Sahl, concerning His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses﴾, to the end of the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the voluntary prayers in the houses of his wives, by night and by day." (p-1170)

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 33, verses 28–34 (part 1 of 3):

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾. It has been said: this verse is connected in meaning with what precedes it, namely the prohibition of harming the Prophet (ﷺ), for he had been harmed by some of his wives.

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes (mufassirun) said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) asked him for some of the goods of this world, and they requested an increase in maintenance (nafaqah), and they harmed him through jealousy of one another. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a vow (ila') against them for a month, and Allah revealed this verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir). They were nine at that time: ʿA'ishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah, Umm Habibah, Sawdah, these being of the women of Quraysh; Safiyyah al-Khaybariyyah; Maymunah al-Hilaliyyah; Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah; and Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah.

The meaning of ﴿the life of this world and its adornment﴾ is its abundance, its splendour, its luxury, and indulgence in it. ﴿Then come, I will provide for you﴾: that is, come towards me, ﴿and I will provide for you﴾ (umatti'kunna) with the jussive as a response to the imperative, meaning: I will give you the provision (mut'ah). And ﴿and release you kindly﴾ (wa usarrihkunna) with the jussive, meaning: I will divorce you. The jussive in both verbs is what the majority (al-jumhur) read. Humayd al-Kharraz read both verbs in the nominative (raf'), as a resumption (isti'naf). The meaning of "kind release" (al-sarah al-jamil) is that which occurs without harm, in accordance with the Sunnah.

It has also been said: the jussive of both verbs is because they are the response to a condition (shart), and on this view ﴿Then come﴾ is a parenthetical clause (i'tiraD) between the condition and its response.

﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾ (p-1166) — that is, Paradise and its blessings — ﴿then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾ — that is, those who did righteous deeds — ﴿a great reward﴾ that cannot be described and whose measure cannot be estimated; and that is because of their goodness and in return for the righteousness of their deeds.

The scholars have differed over the manner in which the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his wives the choice, in two views. The first view: he gave them the choice, by the permission of Allah, between remaining in the marriage or divorce, and they chose to remain. This was the position of ʿA'ishah, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri and Rabi'ah. The second view: he only gave them the choice between this world, whereupon he would part from them, and the Hereafter, whereupon he would keep them, and he did not give them the choice regarding divorce. This was said by ʿAli, al-Hasan and Qatadah. The preponderant (al-rajih) view is the first.

They also differed concerning the woman given the choice: if she chooses her husband, does that mere choice count as a single divorce (talaqah) against the husband or not? The majority of the early and later scholars held that when a woman chooses her husband, it is not a divorce, neither one nor more.

ʿAli and Zayd ibn Thabit said: if she chooses her husband, it is a single irrevocable divorce (ba'inah). This was also said by al-Hasan and al-Layth, and al-Khattabi and al-Naqqash related it from Malik.

The preponderant view is the first, because of the sound hadith of ʿA'ishah in the two Sahihs: "She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us the choice, and we chose him, and he did not count it as a divorce." There is no basis for making the mere choice a divorce. The claim that it is an allusion (kinayah) to divorce is rebutted by the fact that the one who gives the choice did not intend separation by the mere choice, but intended to delegate (tafwid) the woman and place her affair in her own hand. If she chooses to remain, she remains in the state of marriage that she was in; if she chooses separation, she becomes divorced.

They differed over whether her choosing herself is a revocable divorce (talaqah raj'iyyah) or an irrevocable one (ba'inah). Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Abi Layla, al-Thawri and al-Shafi'i said the first; ʿAli, Abu Hanifah and his companions, and a report from Malik, said the second.

The preponderant view is the first, because it is utterly far-fetched that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would divorce his wives contrary to what Allah commanded him, and He commanded him by saying: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [al-Talaq: 1]. It is related from Zayd ibn Thabit that if she chooses herself it is three divorces, but there is no basis for this view.

It is also related from ʿAli that if she chooses herself it is nothing, and if she chooses her husband it is a single revocable divorce.

Then, when the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) chose the Messenger of Allah, Allah revealed these verses concerning them, as an honour for them and an exaltation of their right. He said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency﴾ — that is, manifestly ugly and evidently foul — and Allah had protected them from that, cleared them and purified them. ﴿The punishment will be doubled for her, double﴾ — that is, He will punish them with twice the punishment of other women if they commit the like of that indecency, and that is because of their nobility, the loftiness of their rank and the elevation of their station.

It has been established in this Sharia, in more than one place, that the multiplication of nobility and the elevation of ranks necessitate, for their possessor if he disobeys, the multiplication of punishments.

Abu ʿAmr read "yudaʿaf" (yuḍaʿʿaf) in the passive voice, and he and Abu ʿUbayd distinguished between yudaʿaf and yuḍaʿʿaf, saying: yudaʿaf means three punishments and yuḍaʿʿaf means two punishments.

Al-Nahhas said: this distinction he has brought, no one among the people of the language knows it, and the meaning of yudaʿaf and yuḍaʿʿaf is one: it is made into double. Thus Ibn Jarir's statement, what they both said, is weakened. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾ — it does not burden Him and is not difficult for Him.

﴿And whoever of you is obedient (yaqnut) to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds﴾ — the majority read yaqnut with the yaʾ (taḥtiyyah), and likewise they read ﴿ya'ti minkunna﴾, taking account of the wording of "min" in both places. Al-Jahdari, Ya'qub, Ibn ʿAmir in one narration, and Abu Jaʿfar read it with the tāʾ (fawqiyyah), taking account of the meaning. The meaning of "man yaqnut" is "man yuti'" (whoever obeys). Likewise the readers differed over "mubayyinah": some read it with a kasrah, and some read it with a fathah on the yaʾ, as already mentioned in al-Nisa'.

Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʿAmir read "nadaʿʿif" with the nun and the accusative "al-ʿadhab". "Nuḍaʿif" with a kasrah on the ʿayn was also read, in the active voice. ﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read with the yaʾ, and likewise they read "ya'mal" with the yaʾ; the rest read "ta'mal" with the tāʾ, and "nu'ti" with the nun. The meaning of their being given their reward twice is that they will have, for obedience, twice what other women deserve if they perform that same obedience.

In this there is a strong proof that the meaning of ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, double﴾ is that the punishment will be twice, not thrice, because the purpose is to show their nobility and distinction in obedience and disobedience: their good deed counts as two good deeds, and their evil deed as two evil deeds. Had their evil deed been like three evil deeds, it would not fit that their good deed be like two good deeds, for Allah is too just to multiply the punishment for them to a degree exceeding the multiplication of their reward. ﴿And We have prepared for her﴾, in addition to the double reward, ﴿a generous provision﴾.

The exegetes said: the generous provision is the bounty of Paradise; al-Nahhas related this from them.

Then He, glory be to Him, made their excellence over all other women explicit, saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of the women﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: He did not say "like one of the women," because "ahad" is a general negation applying to the masculine and feminine, the singular and plural. It may be said of what is not human, as one says: "There is no one (ahad) in it, neither sheep nor camel."

The meaning: you are not like a single group among the groups of women in virtue and nobility.

Then He restricted this great nobility by a condition, saying: ﴿if you fear Allah﴾. Thus He, glory be to Him, made clear that this excellence for them is only by their steadfast adherence to piety (taqwa), not by mere connection to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Clear piety, sincere faith, and walking in the manner of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his life and after his death have indeed been found in them, all praise be to Allah.

The response to the condition is omitted, being indicated by what precedes it, meaning: if you fear Allah, then you are not like any one of the women.

It has been said that its response is ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾ (fa-la takhdhna), but the first is preferable.

The meaning of ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾ is: do not make your speech soft when addressing people, as the women of ill repute do, for that causes a great corruption, namely ﴿so that one in whose heart is a disease may covet﴾ — that is, immorality, doubt and hypocrisy. The accusative of "yatma'a" is because it is the response to the prohibition. The majority read it thus.

Abu Hatim related that al-A'raj read "fa-yat'ami'" with a fathah on the yaʾ and a kasrah on the mim. Al-Nahhas said: I reckon this is an error. This reading is related from Abu al-Sammal, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Muhaysin, and it is related from them that they read it in the jussive, coordinated with the position of the prohibitive verb.

﴿And speak a known word﴾ — among the people, far from doubt, according to the ways of the Sharia, such that its hearer finds nothing objectionable in it, and the people of wickedness and immorality do not covet them because of it.

﴿And stay in your houses﴾ (wa-qarna fi buyutikunna). The majority read "wa-qirna" with a kasrah on the qaf, from waqara yaqiru waqaran, meaning: to be settled. The imperative of it is "qir" with a kasrah on the qaf, and for women: "qirna", like "idna" and "zinna".

Al-Mubarrad said: it is from al-qarar, not from al-waqar. You say "qarartu bi-l-makan" with a fathah on the ra', and the original is "iqrirna" with a kasrah on the ra'. The first ra' was dropped for lightness, as they said in "zaliltu" → "zalt", and they transferred its vowel to the qaf, and the hamzat al-wasl was dispensed with by moving the qaf.

Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: the first ra' was changed into a yaʾ out of dislike of gemination, as it was changed in qirat and dinar, and the yaʾ took the vowel of the letter from which it was changed. The underlying form is "iqirna," then the vowel of the yaʾ is cast onto the qaf, out of dislike of moving the yaʾ with a kasrah, so the yaʾ falls for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the hamzat al-wasl falls because what follows it is moved, so it becomes "qarna".

Nafi' and ʿAsim read with a fathah on the qaf, and its root is "qarirtu bi-l-makan" when you stayed in it, with a kasrah on the ra', "aqarru" with a fathah on the qaf, like "hamida yahmadu". This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; Abu ʿUbayd related this from al-Kisa'i, and al-Zajjaj and others mentioned it.

Al-Farra' said: it is like when you say "hal hassta sahibaka," meaning: did you perceive him? Abu ʿUbayd said: our teachers among the people of Arabic used to deny the reading with a fathah on the qaf, because "qarirtu bi-l-makan aqarru" is not permitted by many of the people of Arabic.

The sound form is "qarartu aqirru" with a kasrah, and its meaning is the command to them to be dignified and calm in their houses and not to go out. This contradicts what we have mentioned here from him, from al-Kisa'i, and he is one of his most eminent teachers.

Abu Hatim concurred in denying this reading, saying: "qarna" with a fathah on the qaf has no standing in the language of the Arabs.

Al-Nahhas said: Abu Hatim has been contradicted in his claim that it has no standing in the speech of the Arabs; rather there are two usages in it: one related by al-Kisa'i, and the other from ʿAli ibn Sulayman. As for the usage related by al-Kisa'i, it is what we have already mentioned from the narration of Abu ʿUbayd from him. As for the usage related by ʿAli ibn Sulayman, he said: it is from "qarartu bihi ʿaynan, aqarru," and the meaning: "and be comforted with it in your eyes in your houses." Al-Nahhas said: this is a good form.

I say: it is not good, nor is it the meaning of the verse, for what is intended by it is their being commanded to tranquillity and settling in their houses, and this has nothing to do with the coolness of the eye.

Ibn Abi ʿAblah read "wa-qirna" with an alif of wasl and two ra's, the first with a kasrah according to the original.

﴿And do not display yourselves in the manner of the former time of ignorance (tabarruj al-jahiliyyah al-ula)﴾. Tabarruj is that a woman reveals of her adornment and beauties what she is obliged to cover, of that which excites a man's desire. The meaning of tabarruj has already been mentioned in Surah al-Nur.

Al-Mubarrad said: it is taken from breadth; one says: "in his teeth there is a barej," when they are spaced apart. It has been said: tabarruj is swaggering in walking, but this is very weak.

It has been differed over what is meant by "the former time of ignorance": it has been said: the period between Adam and Noah; it has been said: between Noah and Idris; it has been said: between Noah and Abraham; it has been said: between Moses and Jesus; and it has been said: between Jesus and Muhammad.

Al-Mubarrad said: "al-Jahiliyyah al-Ula" is like saying "al-Jahiliyyah al-Jahla' (the utter ignorance)."

He said: The women of the Jahiliyyah used to display what is ugly to display, to the point that a woman would sit with her husband and her paramour, and her paramour would be alone with what is above the waist-wrap upward, while her husband would be alone with what is below it downward; and at times one of them would ask the other for an exchange.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: What appears to me is that He meant the Jahiliyyah that they had reached, from which they were commanded to shift away from their conduct in it, namely what was before the Sharia of the conduct of the disbelievers, because they had no jealousy (ghayrah) among them. The meaning is not that there is another Jahiliyyah; so he said, and it is a good opinion.

It is possible that by the other Jahiliyyah is meant what occurs in Islam of imitating the people of the Jahiliyyah by word or deed. The meaning then is: "And do not display yourselves, O Muslim women, after your Islam, with a display like the display of the Jahiliyyah in which you were, and which was upon those before you." That is: do not produce, by your actions and your words, a Jahiliyyah resembling the Jahiliyyah that was before. ﴿And establish the prayer, give the zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. He singled out the prayer and the zakah because they are the foundation of the bodily and financial acts of obedience.

Then He generalized, commanding them to obey Allah and His Messenger in everything that is Sharia. ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾. That is: Allah has only enjoined upon you what He has enjoined of piety, that you not be soft in speech, that you speak what is customary (ma'ruf), that you remain in your houses, that you not display yourselves, that you establish the prayer and give the zakah, and obey; so that He may remove from you the impurity, O people of the House. By "ar-rijs" (impurity) is meant sin and wrongdoing, which defile honor, arising from abandoning what Allah has commanded and doing what He has forbidden; so everything in which there is no pleasure of Allah falls under that.

The accusative of "Ahl al-Bayt" is in the sense of praise (al-madh), as al-Zajjaj said; and he said: if you wish, it is in apposition (badal). He said: the nominative and genitive are also permissible.

al-Nahhas said: If it is in the genitive, it is in apposition to the kaf and mim (of "ankum" and "yutahhirakum"). al-Mubarrad objected that apposition from the addressed is not permissible; and it is permissible that it be in the accusative by way of address (nida')... ﴿and purify you with a thorough purification﴾. That is: He will purify you from the filths and defilements with complete purification.

In the metaphor of "rijs" for disobedience, and in following it with "purification," there is an eloquent repulsion from it and a severe deterrence for its doer.

The people of knowledge have differed about the People of the House mentioned in the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the People of the House mentioned in the verse are exclusively the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).

They said: By "the house" is meant the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the dwellings of his wives, due to His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses﴾.

Also, the context concerns the wives, from His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives...﴿ up to His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah and the wisdom; indeed Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Mujahid, Qatadah, and it was reported from al-Kalbi, said that the People of the House mentioned in the verse are: 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn exclusively. Among their proofs is that the address in the verse is with what suits the masculine, not the feminine, namely His saying: "'ankum" and "liyutahhirakum." Had it been exclusively for the women, He would have said "'ankunna" and "yutahhirukunna."

The earlier ones answered this: the masculine is by consideration of the word "Ahl" (people), as He, glorified be He, said: (p-1168) ﴿Do you wonder at the command of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the House﴾ [Hud: 73], and as a man says to his companion: "How is your family?" meaning his wife or wives, and he replies: "They are well."

Let us mention here what each group held to: As for the first, they held to the context, for it concerns the wives as we mentioned, and to what Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) exclusively.

'Ikrimah said: Whoever wishes, I will invoke a mubahalah (mutual curse) with him that it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated similar from the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Ikrimah similar. Ibn Sa'd narrated from 'Urwah similar.

As for what the others held to: al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, through several routes: "From Umm Salamah who said: In my house it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾, and in the house were Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) covered them with a cloak that was upon him, then said: 'These are my People of the House, so remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated "from Umm Salamah also, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in her house on his bed, upon which was a Khaybari cloak. Fatimah came with a pot in which was khazirah (a dish of meat and grain), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Call your husband and your two sons, al-Hasan and al-Husayn,' and she called them. While they were eating, there was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) took the remnant of his cloak and covered them with it, then he extended his hand out of the cloak and raised it toward the sky, then said: 'O Allah, these are my People of the House and my close ones, so remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification,' saying it three times.

Umm Salamah said: I put my head into the curtain and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and am I with you?' He said: 'You are upon goodness, twice.'" Ahmad also narrated it from her narration, saying: "Narrated 'Abdullah ibn Numayr to us, narrated 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman to us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, narrated to me one who heard Umm Salamah mention that the Prophet (ﷺ)..." and he mentioned it.

In its chain is an unknown narrator, who is the teacher of 'Ata', and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.

al-Tabarani also narrated it from her through two routes with similar wording.

Ibn Kathir in his tafsir mentioned for the hadith of Umm Salamah many routes in the Musnad of Ahmad and others.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khatib narrated similar from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.

al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh again narrated from 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, stepson of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: When this verse was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾, and he mentioned something like the hadith of Umm Salamah.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim narrated from 'A'ishah who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) went out one morning wearing a black-haired striped cloak of wool. Al-Hasan and al-Husayn came, and he admitted them with him; then Fatimah came, and he admitted her with him; then 'Ali came, and he admitted him with him; then he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Fatimah, and with him were 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, until he entered. He brought 'Ali and Fatimah near and seated them before him, and seated al-Hasan and al-Husayn each upon one of his thighs. Then he wrapped his garment around them, while I was behind them. Then he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾ and said: 'O Allah, these are my People of the House; O Allah, remove from them the impurity and purify them with a thorough purification.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and am I from your family?' He said: 'And you are from my family.'"

Wathilah said: "Indeed, it is more hopeful than what I hope for." It has routes in the Musnad of Ahmad.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi who graded it hasan, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas: "That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pass by the door of Fatimah when he went out to the dawn prayer, saying: 'The prayer, O People of the House, the prayer! ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾'"

Muslim narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I remind you of Allah regarding my People of the House." It was said to Zayd: "And who are his People of the House? Are not his wives from his People of the House?" He said: "His wives are from his People of the House, but his People of the House are those who are forbidden the charity after him: the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of al-'Abbas."

al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed Allah divided creation into two divisions, and placed me in the better of the two divisions. That is His saying: ﴿And the companions of the right hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 7] ﴿And the companions of the left hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 41]; so I am of the companions of the right, and I am the best of the companions of the right. Then He made the two divisions into thirds, and placed me in the best of them as three. That is His saying: ﴿So the companions of the right hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 8] ﴿and the companions of the left hand﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 9] ﴿and the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 10]; so I am of the foremost, and I am the best of the foremost. Then He made the thirds into tribes, and placed me in the best tribe. That is His saying: ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13]; and I am the most righteous and the most honored of the children of Adam before Allah, and no boast. Then He made the tribes into houses, and placed me in the best house. That is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification﴾. So I and the People of my House are purified from sins.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Hamra' who said: "I stayed in Madinah for seven months during the time of the Messenger of Allah. I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the dawn rose, come to the door of 'Ali and Fatimah and say: 'The prayer, the prayer! ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and purify you with a thorough purification.﴾'"

In its chain is Abu Dawud al-A'ma, who is a fabricator and a liar (wada' kadhdhab).

There are in this chapter hadiths and reports; and we have mentioned here what is suitable to be relied upon, apart from what is not suitable.

A third group has moderated between the two groups, making this verse inclusive of the wives and of 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. As for the wives, it is because they are the ones intended in the context of these verses, as we previously stated, and because they are the ones dwelling in his houses (ﷺ), descending in his dwellings; and what was previously reported from Ibn 'Abbas and others supports this. As for the inclusion of 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, it is because they are his relatives and his People of the House by lineage. What we have mentioned of the hadiths explicitly stating that they were the cause of revelation supports this. Whoever makes the verse exclusive to one of the two groups has acted upon part of what must be acted upon and neglected what must not be neglected.

This view has been preferred by a group of verifiers, among them al-Qurtubi, Ibn Kathir, and others.

And some scholars said: they are the Banu Hashim. They relied on the hadith of Ibn Abbas mentioned earlier, and on the statement of Zayd ibn Arqam mentioned earlier, where he said: "But his family are those who were deprived of charity after him: the family of Ali, the family of Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of al-Abbas." These scholars held that what is meant by "the house" is the house of lineage.

His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾. That is: remember the favour of Allah when He placed you in houses where the verses of Allah and wisdom are recited. Remember them, reflect upon them, so that you may be admonished by the admonitions of Allah. Or remember them for the people, so that they may take admonition from them and be guided by their guidance. Or remember them by reciting them, so that you may memorise them and not cease to recite them frequently.

Al-Qurtubi said: The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said: "The verses of Allah" are the Qur'an, and "wisdom" is the Sunnah (the prophetic practice and teaching).

Muqatil said: What is meant by "the verses and wisdom" is His command and prohibition in the Qur'an.

It was also said: the Qur'an combines being clear verses, indicating the Oneness of God and the truth of prophethood, and being wisdom, comprising various branches of knowledge and laws.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾. That is: Subtle towards His friends, Acquainted with all His creation and with everything that proceeds from them, whether good or evil, obedience or disobedience. He rewards the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.

Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted, through the route of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: "Abu Bakr came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while people were sitting at his door and the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting, but he was not granted permission. Then Umar came and sought permission, but he was not granted permission. Then permission was given to Abu Bakr and Umar, and they entered while the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting with his wives around him, and he was silent. Umar said: 'I will speak to the Prophet (ﷺ), perhaps he will laugh.' Then Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen the daughter of Zayd, the wife of Umar, when she asked me for maintenance a moment ago, and I struck her on the neck.' The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, and said: 'They are around me, asking me for maintenance.' Abu Bakr then got up to Aisha to strike her, and Umar got up to Hafsa, both saying: 'You ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for what he does not have.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them. His wives said: 'By Allah, we will not ask the Messenger of Allah for what he does not have after this gathering.' And Allah revealed the option (of choice). He called Aisha and said: 'I am going to mention to you a matter, and I do not want you to hasten in it until you consult your two parents.' She said: 'What is it?' Then he recited to her ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives...﴾ to the end of the verse. Aisha said: 'Concerning you, should I consult my parents? Rather, I choose Allah and His Messenger, and I ask you not to mention to your wives what I have chosen.' He said: 'Indeed Allah did not send me as one who causes difficulty, but He sent me as a teacher and a bringer of good news. None of them will ask me about what you have chosen except that I will inform her.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "came to her when Allah commanded him to give his wives the choice. She said: He began with me and said: 'I am going to mention to you a matter, and there is no harm for you in not hastening until you consult your two parents.' And he knew that my parents would not have commanded me to separate from him. He said: 'Indeed Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world...﴾' to the end of the verse. I said to him: 'Then in which of these should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode.' And the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) did the same as I did."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And whoever of you is devoutly obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness﴾, that he said: "That is: whoever of you obeys Allah, and whoever of you does deeds for Allah and His Messenger by obeying Him."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him concerning His saying: ﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾, that he said: "That is: do not make your speech alluring, and do not be soft in speech."

Ibn al-Mundhir also transmitted from him, concerning the same verse: "It is the softening of speech with men, until the one in whose heart is a disease becomes eager."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "I was informed that it was said to Sawda, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'What is wrong with you that you do not perform Hajj or 'Umrah as your sisters do?' She said: 'I have performed Hajj and 'Umrah, and Allah has commanded me to remain in my house. By Allah, I will not leave my house until I die.' He said: 'By Allah, she did not leave the door of her chamber until she was carried out on her bier.'"

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Sa'd, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Zuhd, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Masruq, who said: "Whenever Aisha recited ﴿And stay in your houses﴾, she would weep until her head-covering was soaked."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman transmitted: "The first jahiliyya (age of ignorance, the pre-Islamic period of unbelief) was between Noah and Idris, and it was a thousand years."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas that Umar ibn al-Khattab asked him: "Tell me about the saying of Allah to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And do not display yourselves as in the first jahiliyya﴾. Was there more than one jahiliyya?" Ibn Abbas said: "I have not heard of a 'first' except that it has a 'last'." Umar said to him: "Bring me from the Book of Allah what confirms that." He said: "Allah says: ﴿And strive in Allah with the striving due to Him; He has chosen you﴾ [al-Hajj 22:78] as the first time." Umar said: "Who commanded us to strive?" He said: "Makhzum and Abd Shams."

Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning the verse, that he said: "There will be another jahiliyya." Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Aisha that she recited this verse and said: "The first jahiliyya was in the time of Abraham." Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The first jahiliyya was between Jesus and Muhammad."

We have already mentioned the reports concerning the occasion of revelation of His saying: ﴿Allah only desires to remove from you the impurity, O people of the house﴾.

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾, that he said: "It is the Qur'an and the Sunnah (the Prophet's practice), by which He bestows favour upon them."

Ibn Sa'd transmitted from Abu Umama, from Sahl, concerning His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses﴾, to the end of the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the voluntary prayers in the houses of his wives, by night and by day." (p-1170)

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 33, verses 28–34 (part 1 of 3):

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾. It has been said: this verse is connected in meaning with what precedes it, namely the prohibition of harming the Prophet (ﷺ), for he had been harmed by some of his wives.

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes (mufassirun) said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) asked him for some of the goods of this world, and they requested an increase in maintenance (nafaqah), and they harmed him through jealousy of one another. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a vow (ila') against them for a month, and Allah revealed this verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir). They were nine at that time: ʿA'ishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah, Umm Habibah, Sawdah, these being of the women of Quraysh; Safiyyah al-Khaybariyyah; Maymunah al-Hilaliyyah; Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah; and Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah.

The meaning of ﴿the life of this world and its adornment﴾ is its abundance, its splendour, its luxury, and indulgence in it. ﴿Then come, I will provide for you﴾: that is, come towards me, ﴿and I will provide for you﴾ (umatti'kunna) with the jussive as a response to the imperative, meaning: I will give you the provision (mut'ah). And ﴿and release you kindly﴾ (wa usarrihkunna) with the jussive, meaning: I will divorce you. The jussive in both verbs is what the majority (al-jumhur) read. Humayd al-Kharraz read both verbs in the nominative (raf'), as a resumption (isti'naf). The meaning of "kind release" (al-sarah al-jamil) is that which occurs without harm, in accordance with the Sunnah.

It has also been said: the jussive of both verbs is because they are the response to a condition (shart), and on this view ﴿Then come﴾ is a parenthetical clause (i'tiraD) between the condition and its response.

﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾ (p-1166) — that is, Paradise and its blessings — ﴿then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾ — that is, those who did righteous deeds — ﴿a great reward﴾ that cannot be described and whose measure cannot be estimated; and that is because of their goodness and in return for the righteousness of their deeds.

The scholars have differed over the manner in which the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his wives the choice, in two views. The first view: he gave them the choice, by the permission of Allah, between remaining in the marriage or divorce, and they chose to remain. This was the position of ʿA'ishah, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri and Rabi'ah. The second view: he only gave them the choice between this world, whereupon he would part from them, and the Hereafter, whereupon he would keep them, and he did not give them the choice regarding divorce. This was said by ʿAli, al-Hasan and Qatadah. The preponderant (al-rajih) view is the first.

They also differed concerning the woman given the choice: if she chooses her husband, does that mere choice count as a single divorce (talaqah) against the husband or not? The majority of the early and later scholars held that when a woman chooses her husband, it is not a divorce, neither one nor more.

ʿAli and Zayd ibn Thabit said: if she chooses her husband, it is a single irrevocable divorce (ba'inah). This was also said by al-Hasan and al-Layth, and al-Khattabi and al-Naqqash related it from Malik.

The preponderant view is the first, because of the sound hadith of ʿA'ishah in the two Sahihs: "She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us the choice, and we chose him, and he did not count it as a divorce." There is no basis for making the mere choice a divorce. The claim that it is an allusion (kinayah) to divorce is rebutted by the fact that the one who gives the choice did not intend separation by the mere choice, but intended to delegate (tafwid) the woman and place her affair in her own hand. If she chooses to remain, she remains in the state of marriage that she was in; if she chooses separation, she becomes divorced.

They differed over whether her choosing herself is a revocable divorce (talaqah raj'iyyah) or an irrevocable one (ba'inah). Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Abi Layla, al-Thawri and al-Shafi'i said the first; ʿAli, Abu Hanifah and his companions, and a report from Malik, said the second.

The preponderant view is the first, because it is utterly far-fetched that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would divorce his wives contrary to what Allah commanded him, and He commanded him by saying: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [al-Talaq: 1]. It is related from Zayd ibn Thabit that if she chooses herself it is three divorces, but there is no basis for this view.

It is also related from ʿAli that if she chooses herself it is nothing, and if she chooses her husband it is a single revocable divorce.

Then, when the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) chose the Messenger of Allah, Allah revealed these verses concerning them, as an honour for them and an exaltation of their right. He said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency﴾ — that is, manifestly ugly and evidently foul — and Allah had protected them from that, cleared them and purified them. ﴿The punishment will be doubled for her, double﴾ — that is, He will punish them with twice the punishment of other women if they commit the like of that indecency, and that is because of their nobility, the loftiness of their rank and the elevation of their station.

It has been established in this Sharia, in more than one place, that the multiplication of nobility and the elevation of ranks necessitate, for their possessor if he disobeys, the multiplication of punishments.

Abu ʿAmr read "yudaʿaf" (yuḍaʿʿaf) in the passive voice, and he and Abu ʿUbayd distinguished between yudaʿaf and yuḍaʿʿaf, saying: yudaʿaf means three punishments and yuḍaʿʿaf means two punishments.

Al-Nahhas said: this distinction he has brought, no one among the people of the language knows it, and the meaning of yudaʿaf and yuḍaʿʿaf is one: it is made into double. Thus Ibn Jarir's statement, what they both said, is weakened. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾ — it does not burden Him and is not difficult for Him.

﴿And whoever of you is obedient (yaqnut) to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds﴾ — the majority read yaqnut with the yaʾ (taḥtiyyah), and likewise they read ﴿ya'ti minkunna﴾, taking account of the wording of "min" in both places. Al-Jahdari, Ya'qub, Ibn ʿAmir in one narration, and Abu Jaʿfar read it with the tāʾ (fawqiyyah), taking account of the meaning. The meaning of "man yaqnut" is "man yuti'" (whoever obeys). Likewise the readers differed over "mubayyinah": some read it with a kasrah, and some read it with a fathah on the yaʾ, as already mentioned in al-Nisa'.

Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʿAmir read "nadaʿʿif" with the nun and the accusative "al-ʿadhab". "Nuḍaʿif" with a kasrah on the ʿayn was also read, in the active voice. ﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read with the yaʾ, and likewise they read "ya'mal" with the yaʾ; the rest read "ta'mal" with the tāʾ, and "nu'ti" with the nun. The meaning of their being given their reward twice is that they will have, for obedience, twice what other women deserve if they perform that same obedience.

In this there is a strong proof that the meaning of ﴿the punishment will be doubled for her, double﴾ is that the punishment will be twice, not thrice, because the purpose is to show their nobility and distinction in obedience and disobedience: their good deed counts as two good deeds, and their evil deed as two evil deeds. Had their evil deed been like three evil deeds, it would not fit that their good deed be like two good deeds, for Allah is too just to multiply the punishment for them to a degree exceeding the multiplication of their reward. ﴿And We have prepared for her﴾, in addition to the double reward, ﴿a generous provision﴾.

The exegetes said: the generous provision is the bounty of Paradise; al-Nahhas related this from them.

Then He, glory be to Him, made their excellence over all other women explicit, saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of the women﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: He did not say "like one of the women," because "ahad" is a general negation applying to the masculine and feminine, the singular and plural. It may be said of what is not human, as one says: "There is no one (ahad) in it, neither sheep nor camel."

The meaning: you are not like a single group among the groups of women in virtue and nobility.

Then He restricted this great nobility by a condition, saying: ﴿if you fear Allah﴾. Thus He, glory be to Him, made clear that this excellence for them is only by their steadfast adherence to piety (taqwa), not by mere connection to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Clear piety, sincere faith, and walking in the manner of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his life and after his death have indeed been found in them, all praise be to Allah.

The response to the condition is omitted, being indicated by what precedes it, meaning: if you fear Allah, then you are not like any one of the women.

It has been said that its response is ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾ (fa-la takhdhna), but the first is preferable.

The meaning of ﴿so do not be soft in speech﴾ is: do not make your speech soft when addressing people, as the women of ill repute do, for that causes a great corruption, namely ﴿so that one in whose heart is a disease may covet﴾ — that is, immorality, doubt and hypocrisy. The accusative of "yatma'a" is because it is the response to the prohibition. The majority read it thus.

Abu Hatim related that al-A'raj read "fa-yat'ami'" with a fathah on the yaʾ and a kasrah on the mim. Al-Nahhas said: I reckon this is an error. This reading is related from Abu al-Sammal, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Muhaysin, and it is related from them that they read it in the jussive, coordinated with the position of the prohibitive verb.

﴿And speak a known word﴾ — among the people, far from doubt, according to the ways of the Sharia, such that its hearer finds nothing objectionable in it, and the people of wickedness and immorality do not covet them because of it.

﴿And stay in your houses﴾ (wa-qarna fi buyutikunna). The majority read "wa-qirna" with a kasrah on the qaf, from waqara yaqiru waqaran, meaning: to be settled. The imperative of it is "qir" with a kasrah on the qaf, and for women: "qirna", like "idna" and "zinna".

Al-Mubarrad said: it is from al-qarar, not from al-waqar. You say "qarartu bi-l-makan" with a fathah on the ra', and the original is "iqrirna" with a kasrah on the ra'. The first ra' was dropped for lightness, as they said in "zaliltu" → "zalt", and they transferred its vowel to the qaf, and the hamzat al-wasl was dispensed with by moving the qaf.

Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: the first ra' was changed into a yaʾ out of dislike of gemination, as it was changed in qirat and dinar, and the yaʾ took the vowel of the letter from which it was changed. The underlying form is "iqirna," then the vowel of the yaʾ is cast onto the qaf, out of dislike of moving the yaʾ with a kasrah, so the yaʾ falls for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the hamzat al-wasl falls because what follows it is moved, so it becomes "qarna".

Nafi' and ʿAsim read with a fathah on the qaf, and its root is "qarirtu bi-l-makan" when you stayed in it, with a kasrah on the ra', "aqarru" with a fathah on the qaf, like "hamida yahmadu". This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; Abu ʿUbayd related this from al-Kisa'i, and al-Zajjaj and others mentioned it.

Al-Farra' said: it is like when you say "hal hassta sahibaka," meaning: did you perceive him? Abu ʿUbayd said: our teachers among the people of Arabic used to deny the reading with a fathah on the qaf, because "qarirtu bi-l-makan aqarru" is not permitted by many of the people of Arabic.

The sound form is "qarartu aqirru" with a kasrah, and its meaning is the command to them to be dignified and calm in their houses and not to go out. This contradicts what we have mentioned here from him, from al-Kisa'i, and he is one of his most eminent teachers.

Abu Hatim concurred in denying this reading, saying: "qarna" with a fathah on the qaf has no standing in the language of the Arabs.

Al-Nahhas said: Abu Hatim has been contradicted in his claim that it has no standing in the speech of the Arabs; rather there are two usages in it: one related by al-Kisa'i, and the other from ʿAli ibn Sulayman. As for the usage related by al-Kisa'i, it is what we have already mentioned from the narration of Abu ʿUbayd from him. As for the usage related by ʿAli ibn Sulayman, he said: it is from "qarartu bihi ʿaynan, aqarru," and the meaning: "and be comforted with it in your eyes in your houses." Al-Nahhas said: this is a good form.

I say: it is not good, nor is it the meaning of the verse, for what is intended by it is their being commanded to tranquillity and settling in their houses, and this has nothing to do with the coolness of the eye.

Ibn Abi ʿAblah read "wa-qirna" with an alif of wasl and two ra's, the first with a kasrah according to the original.

﴿And do not display yourselves in the manner of the former time of ignorance (tabarruj al-jahiliyyah al-ula)﴾. Tabarruj is that a woman reveals of her adornment and beauties what she is obliged to cover, of that which excites a man's desire. The meaning of tabarruj has already been mentioned in Surah al-Nur.

Al-Mubarrad said: it is taken from breadth; one says: "in his teeth there is a barej," when they are spaced apart. It has been said: tabarruj is swaggering in walking, but this is very weak.

It has been differed over what is meant by "the former time of ignorance": it has been said: the period between Adam and Noah; it has been said: between Noah and Idris; it has been said: between Noah and Abraham; it has been said: between Moses and Jesus; and it has been said: between Jesus and Muhammad.

Al-Mubarrad said: "al-Jahiliyyah al-Ula" is like saying "al-Jahiliyyah al-Jahla' (the utter ignorance)."

He said: The women of the Jahiliyyah used to display what is ugly to display, to the point that a woman would sit with her husband and her paramour, and her paramour would be alone with what is above the waist-wrap upward, while her husband would be alone with what is below it downward; and at times one of them would ask the other for an exchange.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: What appears to me is that He meant the Jahiliyyah that they had reached, from which they were commanded to shift away from their conduct in it, namely what was before the Sharia of the conduct of the disbelievers, because they had no jealousy (ghayrah) among them. The meaning is not that there is another Jahiliyyah; so he said, and it is a good opinion.

It is possible that by the other Jahiliyyah is meant what occurs in Islam of imitating the people of the Jahiliyyah by word or deed. The meaning then is: "And do not display yourselves, O Muslim women, after your Islam, with a display like the display of the Jahiliyyah in which you were, and which was upon those before you." That is: do not produce, by your actions and your words, a Jahiliyyah resembling the Jahiliyyah that was before. ﴿And establish the prayer, give the zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. He singled out the prayer and the zakah because they are the foundation of the bodily and financial acts of obedience.

Then He generalized, commanding them to obey Allah and His Messenger in everything that is Sharia. ﴿Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House﴾. That is: Allah has only enjoined upon you what He has enjoined of piety, that you not be soft in speech, that you speak what is customary (ma'ruf), that you remain in your houses, that you not display yourselves, that you establish the prayer and give the zakah, and obey; so that He may remove from you the impurity, O people of the House. By "ar-rijs" (impurity) is meant sin and wrongdoing, which defile honor, arising from abandoning what Allah has commanded and doing what He has forbidden; so everything in which there is no pleasure of Allah falls under that.

The accusative of "Ahl al-Bayt" is in the sense of praise (al-madh), as al-Zajjaj said; and he said: if you wish, it is in apposition (badal). He said: the nominative and genitive are also permissible.

al-Nahhas said: If it is in the genitive, it is in apposition to the kaf and mim (of "ankum" and "yutahhirakum"). al-Mubarrad objected that apposition from the addressed is not permissible; and it is permissible that it be in the accusative by way of address (nida')... ﴿and purify you with a thorough purification﴾. That is: He will purify you from the filths and defilements with complete purification.

In the metaphor of "rijs" for disobedience, and in following it with "purification," there is an eloquent repulsion from it and a severe deterrence for its doer.

The people of knowledge have differed about the People of the House mentioned in the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the People of the House mentioned in the verse are exclusively the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).

They said: By "the house" is meant the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the dwellings of his wives, due to His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses﴾.

Also, the context concerns the wives, from His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives...﴿ up to His saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah and the wisdom; indeed Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾.
