It has been said: those who ask about the Hour are those hypocrites and spreaders of rumours; when they were threatened with punishment, they asked about the Hour, deeming it far-fetched and as a denial. ﴿And what will make you know﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: what will inform you and tell you ﴿that perhaps the Hour is near?﴾, meaning: at a near time. The masculine form is used because the Hour is in the sense of "the day" or "the time," while the feminine of "al-sa'ah" is not real (haqiqi). The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to clarify that if it is hidden from him, he does not know its time, and he is the Messenger of Allah, then how about other people? In this there is a great threat to them.

The word "yawma" (the day) in His words ﴿the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾ is an adverbial accusative (zarf) for His words "they will not find," and it has been said: for "abiding," and it has been said: for "a helper," and it has been said: for an implied verb, which is "remember."

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Umm Salamah who said: When this verse ﴿they draw over themselves some of their jalabib﴾ was revealed, the women of the Ansar went out as if their heads were crows, from the tranquility (sakinah), and upon them were black garments that they wore. Thus it is in the Zawa'id, with the wording "min al-sakinah," and it has no meaning, for the intended meaning is the comparison of the black garments to crows, not that the intended meaning is describing them with tranquility, as one says: "as if upon their heads were birds."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 33, verses 59–68 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿĀʾishah, who said: "May Allah have mercy on the women of the Helpers (al-Anṣār). When the verse ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ was revealed, they tore their woolen cloaks (murūṭ) and wrapped themselves in them, and they prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as if crows were upon their heads."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse, that he said: "A free woman used to wear the clothing of a slave woman, so Allah commanded the believing women that they should draw their outer garments (jalabib) down over themselves. Idnaʾ al-jilbab (drawing down the outer garment) means that she covers herself and fastens it over her forehead."

Ibn Saʿd narrated from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb regarding His saying: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾, that it refers to the hypocrites by their very persons, and ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt, that it refers to the hypocrites also.

Ibn Saʿd also narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Jubayr, who said: "Those in whose hearts is a disease and the agitators (al-murjifūn) in Medina are all the hypocrites."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾, that he said: "We will surely give you power over them."

When al-Shawkani had finished with the rebuke for those among His servants who harm His Messenger and the believing men and women, Allah (glorified is He) commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to instruct some of those who had suffered harm to take a measure that would ward off what befalls them from it. So He said: (p-1184) ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers that they should draw their outer garments (jalabib) over themselves﴾. The word "min" (from) in ﴿min jalabibihinna﴾ is for partitive meaning (li-l-tab'id, "some of"). The word jalabib is the plural of jilbab, which is a garment larger than the khimar (headcover).

Al-Jawhari said: the jilbab is a mulhafa (a wrap or covering cloth). It is also said to be a qina' (veil), and it is also said to be a garment that covers the whole body of the woman, as is established in the Sahih from the hadith of Umm 'Atiyyah, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, one of us may not have a jilbab." He said: "Let her sister clothe her with one of her jilbabs."

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said, they should cover their faces and their heads, except one eye, so that it is known that they are free women and they are not molested.

Al-Hasan said: she covers half of her face.

Qatadah said: she wraps it over the forehead and fastens it, then folds it over the nose; even if her eyes appear, it covers the chest and most of the face.

The reference in His words ﴿dhalika﴾ (that) is to the drawing of the jalabib. It is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is ﴿adna an yu'rafna﴾ (more suitable that they be recognized), meaning: more likely that they will be recognized, so that they are distinguished from slave women, and it becomes apparent to people that they are free women. ﴿So that they will not be harmed﴾ by the people of lewdness through being accosted, with them being watched over, and their families as well. The intended meaning of His words ﴿that they will be recognized﴾ is not that a particular one of them be identified as who she is; rather the meaning is that they be known as free women and not slave women, because they have put on a style of dress that is specific to free women. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what has passed from them of neglecting to draw their jalabib, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them; or, He is Forgiving to the sinners and Merciful to them, so they enter into this by primary inclusion.

Then Allah (glorified is He) threatened the people of hypocrisy and of spreading false rumours, and He said: ﴿If the hypocrites desist not﴾ from what they are upon of hypocrisy, ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt and suspicion about what they are upon of instability, ﴿and those who spread rumours in Al-Madinah﴾ regarding what proceeds from them of spreading rumours, by mentioning false reports that contain the weakening of the side of the Muslims and the ascendancy of the polytheists over them.

Al-Qurtubi said: the exegetes are agreed that the three descriptions refer to one thing, and the meaning is that the hypocrites combined hypocrisy, disease of the hearts, and spreading rumours against the Muslims. So it is, on this view, of the type of the saying:

"To the king, the leader, son of the chief, the lion of the battalion in the crowd"

meaning: to the king, the leader, son of the chief, the lion of the battalion.

'Ikrimah and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: those in whose hearts is a disease are the fornicators (al-zunat).

Al-irjaf in the language is the spreading of lies and falsehood. It is said: arjafa bi-kadha, when he reports it without basis in truth, because it is a report that is unsteady and unestablished, from al-rajfah, which is the earthquake.

It is said: the earth quaked (rajafat al-ard), meaning it moved and convulsed, yartajifu rajfan; and al-rajafan is severe agitation. The sea was named rajjaf because of its agitation. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Those who feed meat every evening, until the sun sets in the rajjaf."

Al-irjaf is the singular of al-arajif (rumours), and arjafu fi al-shay' means they plunged into it. From it is the saying of a poet:

"Though you reproach us with our small number, and a rebel and an envier spread rumours against Islam."

And the saying of another:

"With rumours, O son of baseness, do you threaten me? And in rumours I thought baseness and cowardice."

That is because these spreaders of rumours used to report about the expeditions (saraya) of the Muslims that they had been defeated, and at times that they had been killed, and at times that they had been overcome, and similar things by which the hearts of the Muslims are broken from reports. So Allah (glorified is He) threatened them with His words: ﴿Then We will surely incite you against them﴾, meaning: We will surely empower you over them with killing and dispersal by Our command to you to do so.

Al-Mubarrad said: Allah has indeed incited him against them in His words after this verse:

﴿Cursed; wherever they are found, they shall be seized and massacred with slaughter﴾. So in this there is the meaning of a command to kill them and seize them, meaning: this is their ruling when they remain upon hypocrisy and spreading rumours.

Al-Nahhas said: this is among the best of what has been said regarding the verse.

I say: this is not good, nor is it the best, for His words "cursed..." etc. are merely a supplication against them, not a command to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to fight them, nor an empowerment of him over them. It has been said that they desisted after the revelation of this verse from spreading rumours, so Allah did not incite him against them. The clause ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾ is the answer of the oath (jawab al-qasam), and the clause ﴿Then they will not remain your neighbours therein except briefly﴾ is conjoined to the clause that is the answer of the oath, meaning: they will not be your neighbours therein except for a brief neighbourhood until they perish. The accusative state of mal'unin is a circumstantial accusative (hal), as al-Mubarrad and others said, and the meaning is: expelled, wherever they are found and overtaken. ﴿Seized and massacred﴾ is a supplication against them that they be seized and slain with slaughter. It has been said: this is the ruling regarding them, and it is not a supplication against them; the first is preferable.

It has been said: the meaning of the verse is that they persisted in hypocrisy; for them there was no residence in Al-Madinah except that they were expelled.

﴿A way of Allah with those who passed before, and you will not find for the way of Allah any change﴾. Meaning: Allah has established that in the past nations, namely the cursing of the hypocrites, their seizure, and their slaughter, and likewise the ruling for the spreaders of rumours. It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar).

Al-Zajjaj said: Allah has explained concerning those who act hypocritically toward the prophets and spread rumours against them that they should be slain wherever they are found. ﴿And you will not find for the way of Allah any alteration﴾, meaning: any transformation or change; rather it is established and enduring regarding such people among later and earlier generations.

﴿The people ask you about the Hour﴾, meaning: about the time of its establishment and occurrence. It has been said: those who ask about the Hour are those hypocrites and spreaders of rumours; when they were threatened with punishment, they asked about the Hour, deeming it far-fetched and as a denial. ﴿And what will make you know﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: what will inform you and tell you ﴿that perhaps the Hour is near?﴾, meaning: at a near time. The accusative of qarib (near) is adverbial of time (zarfiyyah). The masculine form is used because the Hour is in the sense of "the day" or "the time," while the feminine of "al-sa'ah" is not real (haqiqi). The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to clarify that if it is hidden from him, he does not know its time, and he is the Messenger of Allah, then how about other people? In this there is a great threat to them.

﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He has expelled them and removed them far from His mercy, ﴿and has prepared for them﴾ in the Hereafter, in addition to that curse from Him upon them in this world, a blaze (sa'ir), meaning: a fire of intense blazing.

﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ without cessation, ﴿they will not find a protector﴾ who would befriend them and protect them from its punishment, ﴿nor a helper﴾ who would help them and rescue them from it.

The word "yawma" (the day) in His words ﴿the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾ is an adverbial accusative (zarf) for His words "they will not find," and it has been said: for "abiding," and it has been said: for "a helper," and it has been said: for an implied verb, which is "remember."

Al-Jumhur read tuqallabu (are turned) with a damma on the ta' and fatha on the lam, in the passive form.

'Isa al-Hamdani and Ibn Abi Ishaq read nuqallibu (We turn) with the nun and a kasra on the lam, in the active form, the agent being Allah (glorified is He).

'Isa also read (p-1185) with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the lam, meaning: the blaze turns their faces.

Abu Haywah, Abu Ja'far and Shaybah read with a fatha on the ta' and the lam, meaning: tatagallabu (they turn about). The meaning of this turning mentioned in the verse is: its turning them at times on one side and at other times on another side, back to belly; or the change of their colours by the scorching of the fire, so that they blacken at times and turn green at others; or the replacement of their skins with other skins. Then at that time ﴿they will say: "O would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger"﴾. The clause is resumptive (mustanafah), as if it was said: what is their state? It was said: they will say. It is also permissible that the meaning be: they will say on the day their faces are turned in the Fire, "O would that we had obeyed Allah..." etc.

They wished that they had obeyed Allah and the Messenger and believed in what he brought, so that they might be saved from what they are in of punishment, as the believers were saved.

The alif in "al-Rasula" and the alif that will come in "al-sabila" are the alif that occurs at the ends of verses (fawasil), which the grammarians call alif al-itlaq (the alif of extension). The explanation of this was already given at the beginning of this surah.

﴿And they will say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders"﴾. This clause is conjoined to the first clause. The intended meaning of "masters" (sada) and "elders" (kubara') is the leaders and chiefs whose command they used to follow in this world and whom they imitated. In this there is a severe warning against blind following (taqlid), and how many are the reminders, warnings and admonitions against this in the Mighty Book, but for one who understands the meaning of Allah's speech, follows it, and is fair to himself, not for one who is of the sort of cattle, in poor understanding, excessive dullness, and extreme partisanship.

Al-Hasan and Ibn 'Amir read "sadatana" (our masters) with a kasra on the ta', the plural of sadah, so it is a plural of a plural.

Muqatil said: they are the ones who gave food at the Battle of Badr. The first is preferable, and there is no basis for restricting it to a specific group. ﴿So they led us astray from the way﴾, meaning: from the path, by what they made attractive to us of disbelief in Allah and His Messenger. The way is monotheism (al-tawhid).

Then they called upon them (for punishment) at that station, saying: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment﴾, meaning: like our punishment, twice over.

Qatadah said: the punishment of this world and the Hereafter. It has been said: the punishment of disbelief and the punishment of misguidance. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾. Al-Jumhur read kathiran (many) with the thaa' (ثاء), meaning: a curse many in number, great in measure, severe in effect. Abu Hatim, Abu 'Ubayd and al-Nahhas preferred this reading. Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Yahya ibn Wathhab, and 'Asim read kabiran with the bi' (ب), meaning: great in itself, severe upon them, heavy in effect.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others have narrated from 'A'ishah that she said: "Sawdah went out after the hijab had been imposed, for her need, and she was a large woman whom no one who knew her could fail to recognize. 'Umar saw her and said: 'O Sawdah, by Allah, you are not hidden from us, so look at how you go out.' She said: So she turned back, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in my house, eating his supper, and in his hand was a bone (ʿarq). She entered and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I went out for some of my need, and 'Umar said to me such and such.' Then revelation came to him, and then it was lifted from him, and the bone was still in his hand, which he had not put down. He said: 'Indeed, it has been permitted for you to go out for your needs.'"

meaning: to the king, the leader, son of the chief, the lion of the battalion.

Al-irjaf is the singular of al-arajif (rumours), and arjafu fi al-shay' means they plunged into it. From it is the saying of a poet:

Al-Nahhas said: this is among the best of what has been said regarding the verse.

It has been said: the meaning of the verse is that they persisted in hypocrisy; for them there was no residence in Al-Madinah except that they were expelled.

The word "yawma" (the day) in His words ﴿the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾ is an adverbial accusative (zarf) for His words "they will not find," and it has been said: for "abiding," and it has been said: for "a helper," and it has been said: for an implied verb, which is "remember."

It has been said: the meaning of the verse is that they persisted in hypocrisy; for them there was no residence in Al-Madinah except that they were expelled.

﴿A way of Allah with those who passed before, and you will not find for the way of Allah any change﴾. Meaning: Allah has established that in the past nations, namely the cursing of the hypocrites, their seizure, and their slaughter, and likewise the ruling for the spreaders of rumours. It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar).

The accusative of qarib (near) is adverbial of time (zarfiyyah). The masculine form is used because the Hour is in the sense of "the day" or "the time," while the feminine of "al-sa'ah" is not real (haqiqi). The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to clarify that if it is hidden from him, he does not know its time, and he is the Messenger of Allah, then how about other people? In this there is a great threat to them.

The word "yawma" (the day) in His words ﴿the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾ is an adverbial accusative (zarf) for His words "they will not find," and it has been said: for "abiding," and it has been said: for "a helper," and it has been said: for an implied verb, which is "remember."

Al-Jumhur read tuqallabu (are turned) with a damma on the ta' and fatha on the lam, in the passive form.

'Isa al-Hamdani and Ibn Abi Ishaq read nuqallibu (We turn) with the nun and a kasra on the lam, in the active form, the agent being Allah (glorified is He).

'Isa also read (p-1185) with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the lam, meaning: the blaze turns their faces.

Abu Haywah, Abu Ja'far and Shaybah read with a fatha on the ta' and the lam, meaning: tatagallabu (they turn about). The meaning of this turning mentioned in the verse is: its turning them at times on one side and at other times on another side, back to belly; or the change of their colours by the scorching of the fire, so that they blacken at times and turn green at others; or the replacement of their skins with other skins. Then at that time ﴿they will say: "O would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger"﴾. The clause is resumptive (mustanafah), as if it was said: what is their state? The reference in His words ﴿dhalika﴾ (that) is to the drawing of the jalabib. It is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is ﴿adna an yu'rafna﴾ (more suitable that they be recognized), meaning: more likely that they will be recognized, so that they are distinguished from slave women, and it becomes apparent to people that they are free women. ﴿So that they will not be harmed﴾ by the people of lewdness through being accosted, with them being watched over, and their families as well. The intended meaning of His words ﴿that they will be recognized﴾ is not that a particular one of them be identified as who she is; rather the meaning is that they be known as free women and not slave women, because they have put on a style of dress that is specific to free women. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what has passed from them of neglecting to draw their jalabib, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them; or, He is Forgiving to the sinners and Merciful to them, so they enter into this by primary inclusion.

Then Allah (glorified is He) threatened the people of hypocrisy and of spreading false rumours, and He said: ﴿If the hypocrites desist not﴾ from what they are upon of hypocrisy, ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt and suspicion about what they are upon of instability, ﴿and those who spread rumours in Al-Madinah﴾ regarding what proceeds from them of spreading rumours, by mentioning false reports that contain the weakening of the side of the Muslims and the ascendancy of the polytheists over them.

Al-Qurtubi said: the exegetes are agreed that the three descriptions refer to one thing, and the meaning is that the hypocrites combined hypocrisy, disease of the hearts, and spreading rumours against the Muslims. So it is, on this view, of the type of the saying:

"To the king, the leader, son of the chief, the lion of the battalion in the crowd"

meaning: to the king, the leader, son of the chief, the lion of the battalion.

'Ikrimah and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: those in whose hearts is a disease are the fornicators (al-zunat).

Al-irjaf in the language is the spreading of lies and falsehood. It is said: arjafa bi-kadha, when he reports it without basis in truth, because it is a report that is unsteady and unestablished, from al-rajfah, which is the earthquake.

It is said: the earth quaked (rajafat al-ard), meaning it moved and convulsed, yartajifu rajfan; and al-rajafan is severe agitation. The sea was named rajjaf because of its agitation. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Those who feed meat every evening, until the sun sets in the rajjaf."

Al-irjaf is the singular of al-arajif (rumours), and arjafu fi al-shay' means they plunged into it. From it is the saying of a poet:

"Though you reproach us with our small number, and a rebel and an envier spread rumours against Islam."

And the saying of another:

"With rumours, O son of baseness, do you threaten me? And in rumours I thought baseness and cowardice."

That is because these spreaders of rumours used to report about the expeditions (saraya) of the Muslims that they had been defeated, and at times that they had been killed, and at times that they had been overcome, and similar things by which the hearts of the Muslims are broken from reports. So Allah (glorified is He) threatened them with His words: ﴿Then We will surely incite you against them﴾, meaning: We will surely empower you over them with killing and dispersal by Our command to you to do so.

Al-Mubarrad said: Allah has indeed incited him against them in His words after this verse:

﴿Cursed; wherever they are found, they shall be seized and massacred with slaughter﴾. So in this there is the meaning of a command to kill them and seize them, meaning: this is their ruling when they remain upon hypocrisy and spreading rumours.

Al-Nahhas said: this is among the best of what has been said regarding the verse.

I say: this is not good, nor is it the best, for His words "cursed..." etc. are merely a supplication against them, not a command to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to fight them, nor an empowerment of him over them. It has been said that they desisted after the revelation of this verse from spreading rumours, so Allah did not incite him against them. The clause ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾ is the answer of the oath (jawab al-qasam), and the clause ﴿Then they will not remain your neighbours therein except briefly﴾ is conjoined to the clause that is the answer of the oath, meaning: they will not be your neighbours therein except for a brief neighbourhood until they perish. The accusative state of mal'unin is a circumstantial accusative (hal), as al-Mubarrad and others said, and the meaning is: expelled, wherever they are found and overtaken. ﴿Seized and massacred﴾ is a supplication against them that they be seized and slain with slaughter. It has been said: this is the ruling regarding them, and it is not a supplication against them; the first is preferable.

It has been said: the meaning of the verse is that they persisted in hypocrisy; for them there was no residence in Al-Madinah except that they were expelled.

﴿A way of Allah with those who passed before, and you will not find for the way of Allah any change﴾. Meaning: Allah has established that in the past nations, namely the cursing of the hypocrites, their seizure, and their slaughter, and likewise the ruling for the spreaders of rumours. It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar).

Al-Zajjaj said: Allah has explained concerning those who act hypocritically toward the prophets and spread rumours against them that they should be slain wherever they are found. ﴿And you will not find for the way of Allah any alteration﴾, meaning: any transformation or change; rather it is established and enduring regarding such people among later and earlier generations.

﴿The people ask you about the Hour﴾, meaning: about the time of its establishment and occurrence. It has been said: those who ask about the Hour are those hypocrites and spreaders of rumours; when they were threatened with punishment, they asked about the Hour, deeming it far-fetched and as a denial. ﴿And what will make you know﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: what will inform you and tell you ﴿that perhaps the Hour is near?﴾, meaning: at a near time. The accusative of qarib (near) is adverbial of time (zarfiyyah). The masculine form is used because the Hour is in the sense of "the day" or "the time," while the feminine of "al-sa'ah" is not real (haqiqi). The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to clarify that if it is hidden from him, he does not know its time, and he is the Messenger of Allah, then how about other people? In this there is a great threat to them.

﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He has expelled them and removed them far from His mercy, ﴿and has prepared for them﴾ in the Hereafter, in addition to that curse from Him upon them in this world, a blaze (sa'ir), meaning: a fire of intense blazing.

﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ without cessation, ﴿they will not find a protector﴾ who would befriend them and protect them from its punishment, ﴿nor a helper﴾ who would help them and rescue them from it.

The word "yawma" (the day) in His words ﴿the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾ is an adverbial accusative (zarf) for His words "they will not find," and it has been said: for "abiding," and it has been said: for "a helper," and it has been said: for an implied verb, which is "remember."

Al-Jumhur read tuqallabu (are turned) with a damma on the ta' and fatha on the lam, in the passive form.

'Isa al-Hamdani and Ibn Abi Ishaq read nuqallibu (We turn) with the nun and a kasra on the lam, in the active form, the agent being Allah (glorified is He).

'Isa also read (p-1185) with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the lam, meaning: the blaze turns their faces.

Abu Haywah, Abu Ja'far and Shaybah read with a fatha on the ta' and the lam, meaning: tatagallabu (they turn about). The meaning of this turning mentioned in the verse is: its turning them at times on one side and at other times on another side, back to belly; or the change of their colours by the scorching of the fire, so that they blacken at times and turn green at others; or the replacement of their skins with other skins. Then at that time ﴿they will say: "O would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger"﴾. The clause is resumptive (mustanafah), as if it was said: what is their state? It was said: they will say. It is also permissible that the meaning be: they will say on the day their faces are turned in the Fire, "O would that we had obeyed Allah..." etc.

They wished that they had obeyed Allah and the Messenger and believed in what he brought, so that they might be saved from what they are in of punishment, as the believers were saved.

The alif in "al-Rasula" and the alif that will come in "al-sabila" are the alif that occurs at the ends of verses (fawasil), which the grammarians call alif al-itlaq (the alif of extension). The explanation of this was already given at the beginning of this surah.

﴿And they will say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders"﴾. This clause is conjoined to the first clause. The intended meaning of "masters" (sada) and "elders" (kubara') is the leaders and chiefs whose command they used to follow in this world and whom they imitated. In this there is a severe warning against blind following (taqlid), and how many are the reminders, warnings and admonitions against this in the Mighty Book, but for one who understands the meaning of Allah's speech, follows it, and is fair to himself, not for one who is of the sort of cattle, in poor understanding, excessive dullness, and extreme partisanship.

Al-Hasan and Ibn 'Amir read "sadatana" (our masters) with a kasra on the ta', the plural of sadah, so it is a plural of a plural.

Muqatil said: they are the ones who gave food at the Battle of Badr. The first is preferable, and there is no basis for restricting it to a specific group. ﴿So they led us astray from the way﴾, meaning: from the path, by what they made attractive to us of disbelief in Allah and His Messenger. The way is monotheism (al-tawhid).

Then they called upon them (for punishment) at that station, saying: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment﴾, meaning: like our punishment, twice over.

Qatadah said: the punishment of this world and the Hereafter. It has been said: the punishment of disbelief and the punishment of misguidance. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾. Al-Jumhur read kathiran (many) with the thaa' (ثاء), meaning: a curse many in number, great in measure, severe in effect. Abu Hatim, Abu 'Ubayd and al-Nahhas preferred this reading. Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Yahya ibn Wathhab, and 'Asim read kabiran with the bi' (ب), meaning: great in itself, severe upon them, heavy in effect.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others have narrated from 'A'ishah that she said: "Sawdah went out after the hijab had been imposed, for her need, and she was a large woman whom no one who knew her could fail to recognize. 'Umar saw her and said: 'O Sawdah, by Allah, you are not hidden from us, so look at how you go out.' She said: So she turned back, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in my house, eating his supper, and in his hand was a bone (ʿarq). She entered and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I went out for some of my need, and 'Umar said to me such and such.' Then revelation came to him, and then it was lifted from him, and the bone was still in his hand, which he had not put down. He said: 'Indeed, it has been permitted for you to go out for your needs.'"

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa'd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Malik who said: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to go out at night for their needs, and some of the hypocrites used to accost them, and they would be harmed. It was said to the hypocrites, and they said: "We only do that with slave women." So this verse was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: a man from the hypocrites used to accost the women of the believers and harm them. When it was said to him, he said: "I thought she was a slave woman." So Allah commanded them to differ from the dress of slave women and to draw their jalabib over themselves, covering their faces except one of their eyes. ﴿That is more suitable that they will be recognized﴾: he says, that is more fitting that they will be recognized.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse that he said: Allah commanded the women of the believers, when they went out of their houses for some need, to cover their faces from above their heads with the jalabib, and to show one eye.

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Umm Salamah who said: When this verse ﴿they draw over themselves some of their jalabib﴾ was revealed, the women of the Ansar went out as if their heads were crows, from the tranquility (sakinah), and upon them were black garments that they wore. Thus it is in the Zawa'id, with the wording "min al-sakinah," and it has no meaning, for the intended meaning is the comparison of the black garments to crows, not that the intended meaning is describing them with tranquility, as one says: "as if upon their heads were birds."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 33, verses 59–68 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿĀʾishah, who said: "May Allah have mercy on the women of the Helpers (al-Anṣār). When the verse ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ was revealed, they tore their woolen cloaks (murūṭ) and wrapped themselves in them, and they prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as if crows were upon their heads."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse, that he said: "A free woman used to wear the clothing of a slave woman, so Allah commanded the believing women that they should draw their outer garments (jalabib) down over themselves. Idnaʾ al-jilbab (drawing down the outer garment) means that she covers herself and fastens it over her forehead."

Ibn Saʿd narrated from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb regarding His saying: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾, that it refers to the hypocrites by their very persons, and ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt, that it refers to the hypocrites also.

Ibn Saʿd also narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Jubayr, who said: "Those in whose hearts is a disease and the agitators (al-murjifūn) in Medina are all the hypocrites."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾, that he said: "We will surely give you power over them."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 33, verses 69–73 (part 1 of 2)**

His statement: ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses﴾ refers to their saying that he had a hernia (udrah), or leprosy (baras), or a defect. Its explanation will come at the end of the discussion. This verse contains a rebuke to the believers and a warning against engaging in any of the matters that harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Muqatil said: Allah admonished the believers not to harm Muhammad (ﷺ) as the Children of Israel harmed Moses.

There was disagreement over what our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was harmed with, until this verse was revealed. Al-Naqqash reported that their harming of Muhammad consisted of their saying, "Zayd ibn Muhammad."

Abu Wa'il said: "He (ﷺ) distributed a share, and a man from the Ansar said: 'This is a distribution in which the face of Allah was not intended.'" It was also said that the verse was revealed concerning the story of Zayd ibn Harithah and Zaynab bint Jahsh, and what was heard about them of people's talk. The meaning of ﴿and he was honorable (wajihan) in the sight of Allah﴾ is: he was great in the sight of Allah, possessing high standing. The one who is wajih (honored) in the sight of Allah is the one of great rank and elevated station. It was also said that, in explaining the wajahah (honor), Allah spoke to him directly.

The majority read ﴿and he was in the sight of Allah﴾ with the letter nun, as a figurative adverbial expression of place. Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, and Abu Haywah read it as "ʿAbd Allāh" with the letter ba (بِالباءِ), from ʿubūdiyyah (servitude). In His saying ﴿so Allah cleared him of what they said﴾, the "mā" (ما) is either a relative pronoun or a verbal-noun particle, meaning: from that which they said.

Or it refers to His saying ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾, meaning: in every matter. ﴿And speak a word of rectitude (qawlan sadidan)﴾ means: a correct and true word.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: this means, speak a word of rectitude concerning Zayd and Zaynab, and do not attribute to the Prophet (ﷺ) anything that is not permissible.

ʿIkrimah said: the word of rectitude is "There is no god but Allah."

It was said: it is that whose outward expression agrees with its inward meaning. It was also said: it is that which is intended for the face of Allah alone. It was further said: it is reconciliation between people.

The word sadid is derived from "tasdid al-sahm", the aiming of an arrow so that the target is hit. The apparent meaning of the verse is that He commanded them to speak a word of rectitude in everything they do and leave undone, so this is not restricted to one type over another. Even if the wording does not explicitly imply generality, the context conveys this meaning, because He, Glorified is He, guided His servants to speak in a way that opposes the speech of the people of harm.

Then He mentioned the reward for those who complied with the command to piety and the word of rectitude, saying: ﴿He will amend for you your deeds﴾, meaning: He will make them righteous rather than corrupt, by guiding them to it and enabling them to do it. ﴿And forgive you your sins﴾, meaning: He will make them expiated and forgiven. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ in doing what is obedience and avoiding what is disobedience, ﴿has certainly attained a great attainment﴾, meaning: he has gained good with a great gain, and has achieved the good of this world and the Hereafter. This sentence is a new independent clause that confirms what came before it.

Then, after He, Glorified is He, finished explaining what is due to the people of obedience of good, after explaining what is due to the people of disobedience of punishment, He explained the greatness of the status of the legal obligations and the difficulty of their matter, saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it﴾.

There is disagreement regarding the interpretation of this "trust" mentioned here. Al-Wahidi said: the meaning of the trust here, according to the consensus of all the exegetes (mufassirun), is obedience and the obligations, on the performance of which reward depends, and on neglecting which punishment is due.

Al-Qurtubi said: the trust encompasses all the attributes of the religion according to the most correct opinions, and this is the view of the majority.

Some of its details have been disputed. Ibn Mas'ud said: it refers to the trust of property, such as deposits and other things. It was also reported from him that it refers to all the obligations, and the most severe of them is the trust of property.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: among the trust is that a woman is entrusted with her private part.

Abu al-Darda' said: the ritual bath from major impurity is a trust, and Allah did not entrust the son of Adam with anything of His religion other than it.

Ibn Umar said: the first thing Allah created in man was his private part, and He said: "This is a trust I deposit with you, so do not clothe it except with right. If you guard it, I will guard you."

So the private part is a trust, the ear is a trust, the eye is a trust, the tongue is a trust, the belly is a trust, the hand is a trust, and the foot is a trust, and there is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness.

Al-Suddi said: it is the entrusting of Adam with his son Qabil over his son Habil, and Qabil's betrayal of him by killing him.

How far this view is from the truth! I wonder what it was that led al-Suddi to interpret this verse in this way. If it was based on some evidence that guided him, then there is no evidence. This verse is not a narration about past servants, such that he could have some basis for it, and this is more remote than any remoteness and weaker than spider webs. If this interpretation was an application of what the Arabic language requires, then there is nothing in the Arabic language that requires this or obliges that this unrestricted trust be understood as something that existed at the beginning of this world. And if this interpretation is purely from personal opinion, then the Mighty Book is not a target for the manipulation of men's opinions. For this reason a warning has been issued against whoever interprets the Qur'an by his own opinion. So beware, O seeker of truth, of accepting such interpretations, and hold firmly to your interpretation of the Book of Allah according to what the Arabic language requires, for it is an "Arabic Qur'an," as Allah described it. If the interpretation comes from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), do not turn to anything else. When the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified. Likewise, what comes from the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), for they are among the Arabs, among the people of the language, and among those who combined knowledge of the Arabic language with knowledge of the technical legal terminology. However, if the meaning of a word is broader than what they explained within the Arabic language, then you must add to what the Companion mentioned what the Arabic language and its subtleties require. So take this as a general principle, and you will benefit from it. We have mentioned in the introduction to this tafsir what will guide you to this.

Al-Hasan said: the trust was presented to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, and they said: "And what is in it?" He said to them: "If you do well, I will reward you, and if you do evil, I will punish you." They said: "No."

Mujahid said: when Allah created Adam, He presented it to him, and it was said to him that, and he said: "I have taken it upon myself."

Something similar was reported from others than al-Hasan and Mujahid.

Al-Nahhas said: this view is the one held by the people of tafsir.

It was also said: this trust is what Allah deposited in the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and the rest of the creatures of proofs of His lordship, that they should manifest them, so they manifested them, except for man, who concealed them and denied them.

Thus said some speakers (mutakallimun) who interpreted the Qur'an by their own corrupt opinion, so the meaning of "we offered" (ʿaraḍnā) according to this would be: we made manifest.

A group of scholars said: it is known that inanimate things do not understand or respond, so there must be an assumption of life in them. This "offering" in the verse is an offering of choice, not an offering of obligation.

Al-Qaffal and others said: the offering in this verse is a parable. That is, if the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, despite the greatness of their bodies, were such that they could be obligated, the bearing of the legal obligations would be heavy upon them, because of the reward and punishment in it. That is, the obligation is a great matter, and it is right that the heavens and the earth and the mountains be unable to bear it, ﴿and man bore it, and he was a wrongdoer, ignorant, if he had understood﴾. This is like His saying: ﴿If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain﴾ [al-Hashr: 21].

It was also said: ʿaraḍnā means "ʿāraḍnā" (we presented in opposition), that is: We presented the trust in opposition to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, so these things were too weak for the trust, and the trust outweighed them by its weight.

It was also said: the offering of the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains was only from Adam (peace be upon him), and that Allah commanded him to present it to them. This is also distortion, not tafsir.

The meaning of ﴿and man bore it﴾ is: he undertook its right, and in that he was a wrongdoer to himself, ignorant of what it required of him, or ignorant of the extent of what he entered into, as Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, or ignorant of his Lord, as al-Hasan said.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "hamalaha" (bore it) is: he betrayed it. He applied the verse to the disbelievers, the transgressors, and the disobedient. It was also said: the meaning of "hamalaha" is: he was obligated to it and bound by it, or he became prepared for it by nature, or he bore it at the time it was presented to him in the realm of atoms (ʿālam al-dharr), when the descendants of Adam came out of his back and the covenant was taken from them.

The lam in ﴿so that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ is connected to "hamalaha" (bore it), meaning: man bore it so that Allah would punish the disobedient and reward the obedient.

On this view, the clause ﴿indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ is a parenthetical insertion between the clause and its purpose, to indicate his failure to fulfill what he bore.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: so that He may punish them for what they betrayed of the trust, what they denied of the messengers, and what they broke of the covenant which they acknowledged when they were brought out of the back of Adam.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: these punished ones are those who betrayed it, and those whom Allah forgives are those who fulfilled it.

Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, We presented that so that the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the polytheism of the polytheist would become manifest, so that Allah would punish them both, and the faith of the believer would become manifest, so that Allah would turn to him, that is, return to him with forgiveness and mercy, if he falls short in some acts of obedience. For this reason it is mentioned with the word "tawbah" (repentance), which indicates that the believing disobedient person is outside of punishment. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, abundant in forgiveness and mercy toward the believers among His servants when they fall short in something that is obligatory upon them.

It has been said that the intended meaning of the trust is reason (ʿaql). But the preferred view is what we have already mentioned from the majority. Whatever else is said is not free from weakness, since it does not conform to the Arabic meaning, nor does it fit what the Sharia requires, nor does it agree with what the definition of the trust requires.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Moses was a shy man, very modest, and none of his skin was seen out of shyness. So those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He only conceals himself this much because of a defect in his skin, either leprosy, or a hernia, or some affliction.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wanted to clear Moses of what they said. So one day he went off alone, took off his clothes upon a rock, and bathed. When he finished, he came forward to take his clothes, but the rock ran off with his garment. Moses took his staff and went after the rock, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he reached a group of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, the most beautiful creation of Allah, and Allah cleared him of what they said. The rock stopped, and he took his garment and put it on, and began striking the rock with his staff. By Allah, there were marks on the rock from his striking it, three or four or five times."

Al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Anbari, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Anas.

Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses﴾, he said: His people said he had a hernia (adar). One day he went out to bathe, and placed his clothes on a rock. The rock ran off with his clothes, and Moses went out after it naked until it brought him to the gatherings of the Children of Israel. They saw him, and he was not a man with a hernia. That is His saying: ﴿So Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.﴾

Al-Hakim narrated it and declared it sound, through the route of al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and a number of the Companions, that God revealed to Musa: "I am going to cause Harun to die, so bring him to such-and-such a mountain." So they set out toward the mountain, and there they found a tree, and a house in which there was a couch with bedding upon it, and a pleasant fragrance. When Harun looked at that mountain, and at the house and what was in it, it pleased him, and he said: "O Musa, I would love to sleep on this couch." Musa said: "Sleep on it." He said: "Sleep with me." So when they both slept, death seized Harun. When he was taken, that house was lifted up, the tree disappeared, and the couch was raised to the heaven. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel, they said: "He killed Harun." Envy of the love the Children of Israel had for him moved them, for Harun was gentler and more lenient with them, while there was some harshness in Musa toward them. When this reached him, he said: "Woe to you! He was my brother; do you think I would kill him?" When they insisted upon it, he stood, prayed two rak'ahs, then supplicated God, and the couch descended with them until they saw it between the heaven and the earth, and so they believed him.

For this reason a warning has been issued against whoever interprets the Qur'an by his own opinion. So beware, O seeker of truth, of accepting such interpretations, and hold firmly to your interpretation of the Book of Allah according to what the Arabic language requires, for it is an "Arabic Qur'an," as Allah described it. If the interpretation comes from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), do not turn to anything else. When the river of Allah comes, the river of Ma'qil is nullified. Likewise, what comes from the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), for they are among the Arabs, among the people of the language, and among those who combined knowledge of the Arabic language with knowledge of the technical legal terminology. However, if the meaning of a word is broader than what they explained within the Arabic language, then you must add to what the Companion mentioned what the Arabic language and its subtleties require. So take this as a general principle, and you will benefit from it. We have mentioned in the introduction to this tafsir what will guide you to this.

Al-Hasan said: the trust was presented to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, and they said: "And what is in it?" He said to them: "If you do well, I will reward you, and if you do evil, I will punish you." They said: "No."

Mujahid said: when Allah created Adam, He presented it to him, and it was said to him that, and he said: "I have taken it upon myself."

Something similar was reported from others than al-Hasan and Mujahid.

Al-Nahhas said: this view is the one held by the people of tafsir.

It was also said: this trust is what Allah deposited in the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and the rest of the creatures of proofs of His lordship, that they should manifest them, so they manifested them, except for man, who concealed them and denied them.

Thus said some speakers (mutakallimun) who interpreted the Qur'an by their own corrupt opinion, so the meaning of "we offered" (ʿaraḍnā) according to this would be: we made manifest.

A group of scholars said: it is known that inanimate things do not understand or respond, so there must be an assumption of life in them. This "offering" in the verse is an offering of choice, not an offering of obligation.

Al-Qaffal and others said: the offering in this verse is a parable. That is, if the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, despite the greatness of their bodies, were such that they could be obligated, the bearing of the legal obligations would be heavy upon them, because of the reward and punishment in it. That is, the obligation is a great matter, and it is right that the heavens and the earth and the mountains be unable to bear it, ﴿and man bore it, and he was a wrongdoer, ignorant, if he had understood﴾. This is like His saying: ﴿If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain﴾ [al-Hashr: 21].

It was also said: ʿaraḍnā means "ʿāraḍnā" (we presented in opposition), that is: We presented the trust in opposition to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, so these things were too weak for the trust, and the trust outweighed them by its weight.

It was also said: the offering of the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains was only from Adam (peace be upon him), and that Allah commanded him to present it to them. This is also distortion, not tafsir.

The meaning of ﴿and man bore it﴾ is: he undertook its right, and in that he was a wrongdoer to himself, ignorant of what it required of him, or ignorant of the extent of what he entered into, as Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, or ignorant of his Lord, as al-Hasan said.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "hamalaha" (bore it) is: he betrayed it. He applied the verse to the disbelievers, the transgressors, and the disobedient. It was also said: the meaning of "hamalaha" is: he was obligated to it and bound by it, or he became prepared for it by nature, or he bore it at the time it was presented to him in the realm of atoms (ʿālam al-dharr), when the descendants of Adam came out of his back and the covenant was taken from them.

The lam in ﴿so that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ is connected to "hamalaha" (bore it), meaning: man bore it so that Allah would punish the disobedient and reward the obedient.

On this view, the clause ﴿indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ is a parenthetical insertion between the clause and its purpose, to indicate his failure to fulfill what he bore.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: so that He may punish them for what they betrayed of the trust, what they denied of the messengers, and what they broke of the covenant which they acknowledged when they were brought out of the back of Adam.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: these punished ones are those who betrayed it, and those whom Allah forgives are those who fulfilled it.

Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, We presented that so that the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the polytheism of the polytheist would become manifest, so that Allah would punish them both, and the faith of the believer would become manifest, so that Allah would turn to him, that is, return to him with forgiveness and mercy, if he falls short in some acts of obedience. For this reason it is mentioned with the word "tawbah" (repentance), which indicates that the believing disobedient person is outside of punishment. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, abundant in forgiveness and mercy toward the believers among His servants when they fall short in something that is obligatory upon them.

It has been said that the intended meaning of the trust is reason (ʿaql). But the preferred view is what we have already mentioned from the majority. Whatever else is said is not free from weakness, since it does not conform to the Arabic meaning, nor does it fit what the Sharia requires, nor does it agree with what the definition of the trust requires.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Moses was a shy man, very modest, and none of his skin was seen out of shyness. So those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He only conceals himself this much because of a defect in his skin, either leprosy, or a hernia, or some affliction.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wanted to clear Moses of what they said. So one day he went off alone, took off his clothes upon a rock, and bathed. When he finished, he came forward to take his clothes, but the rock ran off with his garment. Moses took his staff and went after the rock, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he reached a group of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, the most beautiful creation of Allah, and Allah cleared him of what they said. The rock stopped, and he took his garment and put it on, and began striking the rock with his staff. By Allah, there were marks on the rock from his striking it, three or four or five times."

Al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Anbari, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar from the hadith of Anas.

Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses﴾, he said: His people said he had a hernia (adar). One day he went out to bathe, and placed his clothes on a rock. The rock ran off with his clothes, and Moses went out after it naked until it brought him to the gatherings of the Children of Israel. They saw him, and he was not a man with a hernia. That is His saying: ﴿So Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.﴾

Al-Hakim narrated it and declared it sound, through the route of al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and a number of the Companions, that God revealed to Musa: "I am going to cause Harun to die, so bring him to such-and-such a mountain." So they set out toward the mountain, and there they found a tree, and a house in which there was a couch with bedding upon it, and a pleasant fragrance. When Harun looked at that mountain, and at the house and what was in it, it pleased him, and he said: "O Musa, I would love to sleep on this couch." Musa said: "Sleep on it." He said: "Sleep with me." So when they both slept, death seized Harun. When he was taken, that house was lifted up, the tree disappeared, and the couch was raised to the heaven. When Musa returned to the Children of Israel, they said: "He killed Harun." Envy of the love the Children of Israel had for him moved them, for Harun was gentler and more lenient with them, while there was some harshness in Musa toward them. When this reached him, he said: "Woe to you! He was my brother; do you think I would kill him?" When they insisted upon it, he stood, prayed two rak'ahs, then supplicated God, and the couch descended with them until they saw it between the heaven and the earth, and so they believed him.

And al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) once distributed a portion, and a man said: 'This is a distribution by which the Face of God was not sought.' This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and his face reddened; then he said: 'May the mercy of God be upon Musa; he was harmed with more than this and he was patient.'"

Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) led us in the Zuhr prayer, then said: 'Remain in your places.' Then he came to the men and said: 'God has commanded me to instruct you to fear God and to speak words that are upright.' Then he came to the women and said: 'God has commanded me to instruct you that you fear God and speak words that are upright.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn al-Anbari in his Kitab al-Adda' narrated, from Ibn Abbas, concerning God's words: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust﴾, the verse, that he said: "The Trust is the obligations (fara'id), which God offered to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains: if they fulfilled them, He would reward them, and if they neglected them, He would punish them. They disliked that and feared it, not out of disobedience, but out of reverence for the religion of God, that they should not undertake it. Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it with what it entails, and this is His saying: ﴿And man bore it; indeed, he was wrongdoing and ignorant﴾, meaning: unaware of the command of God."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn al-Anbari in his Kitab al-Adda', and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, narrated from him concerning the verse that he said: "It was presented to Adam, and it was said: 'Take it with what is in it; if you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you.' He said: 'I accept it with what is in it.' And between the 'Asr and the night of that same day, he committed the sin."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir also narrated from him, through another route, something similar.
